svg.text: Глава 31. Методология, политика и стратегии — подробная итоговая шпаргалка
CLAMS • ownership • ticketing • documentation • IaC • environment promotion • DR • policy • SLA • compliance

text.tspan: Culture → shared responsibility.
Lean → incremental progress.
Automation → repeatable change.
Measurement → visible outcomes.
Sharing → reduce knowledge silos.
DevOps is methodology, not one tool/role.
Repeated more than twice → automate candidate.
Not understood → do not automate.
Provisioning, config, promotion, testing, patching.
Choose tool after defining the process/problem.
Version and measure automated change.
One common workflow across IT disciplines.
Acknowledge request, then human review.
Exactly one owner/coordinator per task.
Prioritize, resolve and retain history.
Ownership is not blame.
Short, focused and searchable documentation.
Protect docs while keeping them discoverable.
Define one authoritative source of truth.
IaC keeps desired state and change history together.
Avoid manually duplicated facts.
Separate development, test and production.
Keep environments as identical as practical.
Track configuration changes like application code.
Validate the same change in lower environments first.
Prefer automated tracked production change.
Inventory assets, threats and consequences.
Prioritize services and define recovery sequence.
Replication/failover is not backup.
Keep contacts/procedures/backups available offline.
Assign a recovery leader and exercise the plan.
Policy states required behavior.
Procedure states implementation steps.
SLA states service scope and expectations.
Targets must be measurable with available telemetry.
Policies need consistent enforcement.
Queue factors: organizational impact, security, contract, users, deadline.
Chapter simplified order: many users → one user → enhancement.
Metrics: uptime, resolved tickets, mean resolution time,
SLA objectives met, projects on time/budget, security process adherence.
Environment-specific severity targets need confirmation.
Chapter surveys NIST, ISO, PCI, SOX, HIPAA and other frameworks/laws.
Descriptions are publication-era and largely U.S.-centric.
Current version, jurisdiction and applicability must be verified.
Document policy/licensing concerns and management direction in writing.
Do not treat chapter text as current legal advice.

svg.text: Core: operations succeed when people, process, documentation, automation and measurement reinforce one another.
Traceability and shared ownership matter more than tool branding.
